RaMP-DB multi-database ORA identified 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150) as its top pathway with FDR 1.3e-13, fold enrichment 1429.7, and five steroid hits (testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one/DHT, dehydroepiandrosterone) out of 27 pathway members. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: treatment drives a coordinated perturbation of the steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism network, with five C19/C18 steroids as primary driver metabolites and SAH as a secondary epigenetic/methylation signal. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: the androgen and estrogen steroid hormone metabolism axis. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA identified 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150) as its top pathway with FDR 1.3e-13, fold enrichment 1429.7, and five steroid hits (testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one/DHT, dehydroepiandrosterone) out of 27 pathway members. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked the same KEGG:hsa00140 steroid hormone pathway top-1 with p=8.39e-6. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' as its #1 hit (p=1.68e-4) with a striking 13/13 compound overlap, meaning every input metabolite connected to this pathway — including S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) through its role in SAM-dependent methylation reactions during steroid biosynthesis, and the five steroid hormones themselves as pathway intermediates. The RaMP Reactome entry 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (R-HSA-196071) also ranked in the top 5 (FDR 7.6e-13) with the same five steroid compounds as member hits. Outside the steroid axis, 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) mapped to biopterin metabolism (mummichog, p=0.062) and tyrosine metabolism (p=0.034) — biologically coherent since BH4 is the essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase, the entry-point enzyme of tyrosine biosynthesis. Spermidine and SAH co-hit the 'Urea cycle/amino group metabolism' pathway (mummichog, p=0.034) via their shared polyamine–methylation connection. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: treatment drives a coordinated perturbation of the steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism network, with five C19/C18 steroids as primary driver metabolites and SAH as a secondary epigenetic/methylation signal. BH4 and spermidine represent pathway-adjacent metabolic threads consistent with broader endocrine and amino-acid metabolism crosstalk.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment tools converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00068 as the top-ranked pathway (FDR 1.34e-13, fold enrichment 1429.7), with identical FDR for KEGG:map00150 and REACT:R-HSA-196071; all three databases returned the same five steroid hits with 5/27 overlap. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked KEGG:hsa00140 top-1 with p-value 8.39e-6. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its #1 hit with p-value 8.4e-5 and 13/13 compound overlap, capturing all input metabolites including the non-steroid compounds S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine and spermidine. The five steroid hormones (DHEA, testosterone, DHT, estrone, 17β-estradiol) are primary driver metabolites across all steroid pathways; they serve as substrates or intermediates in the CYP17A1-catalysed conversion steps. Tetrahydrobiopterin independently maps to tyrosine metabolism via mummichog (p 0.058), while S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine and spermidine co-map to urea cycle/amino group metabolism (p 0.058), representing peripheral metabolic threads distinct from the central steroid axis.
